Thanks a lot for your kind response and including my query in the
group.

manager

I will be grateful if you could let me know how to proceed with R
installation/ or if there is any guide on the same for manual
installation along with installation of developer library as mentioned

          }
          clustermat[i,]=colval
       }
        clustmatdf= data.frame(clustermat)
        out<-PCA(input)       rhcollect(reduce.key,out)
   }
)

inputPath<-"/PCAIO"
outputPath<-"/PCAOUT"

           ifolder=inputPath,ofolder=outputPath,
           inout=c('text','text'),jobname="PCA",

messages.subject: Re: Compare RHIPE and RHadoop
messages.body_plain:
I dont think i had anything to ith RHadoop, nor other developers involved in RHIPE.
That said, I find RHIPE better integrated with Hadoop and more extensible.

The following code accesses a HDFS data set each row a JSON (converted to an R list object).
I;m trying to create a data frame with 216 columns in order to perform dimension reduction.

However, there doesn't seem to be a set of variables which not NA for every row( princomp etc drop out rows with NA present  in any column).

Here;s the code, the code in ewrap is nothing hadoop-y or mapreduce-y.

m <- ewrap({
  info <- histosimple <- list()
  ## SimpleMeasurements
  for(i in variables$simpleMeasurements){
    value <- r$simpleMeasurements[[i]][[1]]
    histosimple[[i]] <- NAifNull(value)
  }

  ## Histograms
  for(i in variables$histograms){
    histosimple[[i]] <- summarizeVar(r$histograms[[i]],i)
  }

  nonNAnames <- c()
  for(w in names(histosimple)){
    if(!is.na <http://is.na>(histosimple[[w]])) nonNAnames <- c(nonNAnames,w)
  }
  rhcollect(sort(nonNAnames),1)   # How many rows have % of missing
},before={suppressMessages(library(Hmisc))},trap=TRUE)

z <- rhmr2(map          = m
           ,reduce      = summer
           ,ifolder     = "/user/sguha/telemetry/tmp/workset-topbuilds/p*"
           ,ofolder     = "/user/sguha/telemetry/tmp/variables2"
           ,params      = list(variables=variables,summarizeVar=summarizeVar,NAifNull=function(r) if(is.null(r) || is.infinite(r)) NA else r)
           ,combine     = TRUE)
j <- rhwatch(z)
